record_heading: Rules applied to this file
text: ## Splits (one line each) 1. Which paths need a saved hardest figure: the store's SQL says `hardest_ms IS NULL AND sqin_count > 0` (`record_store.cpp:1519-1520`), the engine's `engine_hardest_ms` (`src/core/model.h:919-933`) takes the largest of every squeeze's difficulty over `act.sqinouts` (squeeze-ins and squeeze-outs) and every E0 fill's difficulty. A path with only a squeeze-out or only an E fill gets a figure at analysis time but is never a candidate for the one-time fill. Test 28 pins the narrow side: `hand_path` sets `sqout_count = 1` on every path (line 1127) and rank 3 (`sqin_count` 0, no figure) is expected to be left out (lines 1154-1158, 1173). The record missed this; it read the SQL's `sqin_count > 0` as the rule without asking the engine. By reading. Which side is right is not in anything I read (D302 says "A squeeze at exactly 0 needs 0.0 ms"); it goes to the user. 2. Which store reads throw on a failing database: D73 item 2 says "Every read throws". Test 25's typed list has eleven reads. The public reads `settled_song_ids` (`record_store.h`, first line of the read list I opened), `rows_missing_hardest` and `hardest_figure_filled` are not in it. The record names the last two; `settled_song_ids` is a third it missed. By reading. 3. A locked database: D72 item 3 says "A database locked by another copy of Hydra fails at once". Test 23 reproduces that on a rollback-journal file (its own comment, lines 984-985: "not WAL, so an exclusive lock keeps readers out"). Hydra's own library file is WAL (test 20 pins it). Test 8 locks a WAL file with a write lock, which a second Hydra can do. Two different lock shapes stand for one decision. By reading. 4. The sentence `hydra_batch` prints for an old file (test 17, lines 796-799) is typed in the test; the record says D115 item 4 calls it "proposed by the executor". Record's near-split holds; I did not reopen D115. 5. `1000` as SQLite's default checkpoint threshold is typed in the production destructor (`record_store.cpp:1036`, "SQLite's own default threshold (D86 item 3)") and twice in test 27 (lines 1099, 1107). Record's finding holds. By reading.

record_heading: Findings that cross records
text: ## Splits (one line each) - Split 1 (the record's, confirmed): two spellings of "is this stamp readable": `StampRule::is_current` (`stored_versions.h:29`, used at `record_store.cpp:448`) and `row_readable_sql()` (`:472-475`, `hyversion IN (accepted...)`, used by the purge at `:1238-1240`). The comment at `:469` says one list feeds both; today the list has one entry, so they cannot differ. - Split 2 (the record's, confirmed): lookup reads other-rules rows Stale (`:449`), the purge keeps them (`:464-467`, `:1233-1234`). D51 call 8 (line 178: "Results made under other rules are kept, and read Ready again when the rules match") backs both halves as one rule. - Split 3 (missed by the auditor): what an old row reads as. A row with a non-current stamp reads Stale (T11, T17, T29). A row with `ms_enabled = -1` reads Not analyzed even with the old stamp "1.6.0" (T30; `record_store.cpp:374-379`). D275 item 5 (line 1353: "Such a database shows "Not analyzed" instead of "Stale"") backs the Not-analyzed answer for 1.5.x and 1.6.x files only. The same sentinel is pinned again in A34 R4 (`test_store_results.cpp:267-269, 290-291`): one verdict should cover T30 and R4. - Split 4 (missed): three answers to "which charts has the batch already done". `settled_song_ids` (Ready plus CantAnalyze; the one production caller, `analysis.cpp:779`), `ready_song_ids` (Ready only; no caller), and the library's Analyzed chip (D79 says the skip list is the chip; I did not open `library_model.cpp`, so I cannot say whether the chip counts a CantAnalyze chart). T21 checks `settled`; T25, T29, T31, T32, T34 and A34 R14/R15 check the uncalled one. Goes to the user with F2. - Split 5 (missed): `Q3` for the same function (`check_profile_fits`) is judged two ways. A33 T4 (Rewrite) and A34 R5/R12 (Keep, disputed in verify/A34.md) test the same refusals; T4 uses the unedited real fixture, R5/R12 hand-edit the record's `ms_limit` and `legacy_fills`. No record proposes a saved expected-output file. T11, T17 and T29 ask for "a copy of a real older-release hydra.db" as an input to read through the store. That is an input file, not an expected-output file, so the ruling at `docs/agents/rulings/code-and-engine.md` line 50 is not touched; I name it so the main session can see the edge.
